newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spot Prods-Gasoline antsy in modest activity.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spot Prods-Gasoline antsy in modest activity.

text.p: U.S. spot refined product differentials showed little movement Monday as nervous gasoline market players kept their eyes on Tosco and Exxon, which have both suffered recent catalytic cracker problems,

New York Harbor traders awaited signs that Tosco's New Jersey cracker had resumed output, while Gulf Coast traders watched for clues regarding the length of time that Exxon's cracker in Baytown, Texas would remain out of service.
On the NYMEX, September gasoline shed 1.37 cent to end at 65.44 cents and September heating oil dipped 0.16 cent to finish at 55.09 cents a gallon.
NEW YORK HARBOR

New York Harbor Gasoline markets remained firm, but buyers held their breaths all day for Tosco, which is said to be in the process of restarting its huge cat cracker in New Jersey, come out selling and prices to crater.
"A couple of people put bids in to them (Tosco) and they didn't even answer," said one trader.

The outcome of the standoff remained unclear since many traders expect Tosco to hold off any selling -- paper and especially cash -- for as long as possible in order to maximize potential profits on its various hedging strategies to stem losses related to the unexpected cat shutdown.

A small amount (less than 25,000 barrels) of "A2" regular reformulated gasoline traded early Monday at 9.00 cents over September NYMEX, but that was the only deal traders said they had heard done all day. An independent trader sold the barrels to a foreign refiner with a large U.S. retail presence.
A2 bids have since backed off to around 8.50 cents over, but offers were hanging tough at 9.00 cents over or even higher for larger amounts.
U.S. GULF

Prompt regular conventional M1 gasoline differentials saw some downward pressure during the day as longs liquidated positions ahead of the schedulig deadline for the front 24th cycle on the Colonial Pipeline, traders said.
Prompt M1 dipped to 0.75 cent under the screen near midday, traders said, a drop of about 0.50 cent on the day, before rebounding modestly late in the day.
Reformulated A1 gasoline differentials saw some weakness during the day, with the prompt barrels talked at about 4.25 cents over the M1 grade, or aboutu 3.90 cents over the NYMEX.

Market players continued to closely eye Exxon's actions in the Gulf markets following the unscheduled outage of its 110,000 barrel per day catalytic cracker. Exxon purchased an estimated one million barrels of conventional gasoline last week.
Some firmness was noted in the heating oil markets, according to traders, where prompt barrels gained about 0.20 cent to sit near 2.30 cents under the September futures price.
MIDCONTINENT

More sellers than buyers continued to push down unleaded gasoline differentials in the Midcontinent following the strong demand for very prompt barrels last week. Improved supply over last week also added to Monday's weakness, traders said.
In the Group Three hub, unleaded gasoline was done at 3.20 cents and 3.50 cents over the Merc, about 0.75 cent below midday levels.
Any months were valued at 1.50 cents over the print.
In Chicago, which traders said seems even better supplied than the Group, unleaded gasoline dropped a penny to 0.00/0.25 cents over the screen.
"There is a perception out there that we are better supplied now," said a Group Three player, noting supplies were at 19-days worth.
Group low sulphur diesel was done at 1.00 cent over the screen, unchanged from Friday.
